checkpoint_8.description: Rival rematch completed; career progression and payout applied.

private_artifact.policy: Hashes only. Savestate and extracted RAM remain outside Git.

rival_result.evidence: career wins 2 -> 3 and career KO count 1 -> 2

training_control.meaning: The mapped boxer attributes did not change during the rival-fight-only transition.

calendar_observation.note: The visible career date advanced three weeks while the contract displayed two weeks until fight. This is valuable for later calendar/scheduling RE but should not yet be interpreted as a bug or a proven formula.

overhaul_relevance: The complete visible training-stat order and persistent RAM layout are now mapped, so further routine training checkpoints have diminishing value unless tracing the writer or derived-overall formula.

The contract/event system can represent a distinct rival event type with custom purse, purse split, promoter cut, lead time, rules, side objective, and opponent identity. These are direct extension points for Career Mode 2.0.
Rival state persists after a rematch and triggers a dedicated post-fight newspaper/narrative event, showing that rivalry is a multi-event career subsystem rather than a one-fight label.

The rival rematch did not create a numeric ranking; Jacob remained UNRANKED at 3-0. The next high-value milestone is the transition to a numeric rank and/or amateur-to-pro progression, not an intentionally engineered loss.
Calendar advancement around contract signing, training, and fight resolution remains unresolved and should be captured at the next progression milestone.
next_capture_priority: Do not spend savestates on routine fights or already-mapped training changes.
Capture the first transition from UNRANKED to a numeric rank.
Capture the amateur-to-pro transition and the offer/event that causes it.
Capture any rival-state change, retirement/removal, or second special rival event.
Capture contract offers when the event type, rank-change promise, number of rounds, sponsor status, weight-class change, or future-contract count differs materially from the current amateur template.
